matrix.cross_device_contract: Remote 0xb680 builds 'G<ch><type><seq>|'; 0xb59c sends/retries/acks. AutoPilot arms 0x200025e1=2 and schedules pending[17] -> single byte 0x23 ('#').

Remote 0xc440 sends 'S|'; AutoPilot schedules event 6 + computes value0 (and value1/bool for extended form) in one pass -> 'P<value0>,' or extended form. Remote has a 'don't downgrade' guard -- a short-form response never overwrites already-stored extended state.
Remote 0xc440 sends '!0|'/'!1|' (mode digit ignored by AutoPilot's dispatch check); AutoPilot's 0x8c70 emits exactly 11 comma-terminated numeric fields.

Remote 0xb958 builds 'I<ch+1><digit>|' with mode digit INVERTED. AutoPilot stores mode verbatim, sets STATE[channel]=5; channel_event_monitor (0x8a80) notices and schedules event 15 with AUTOPILOT_LIVE_POSITION[channel].

Remote FUN_0000b834 sends I9|/I1| (mode byte *0x200018e7), 6 retries over ~1000-3000 ticks. I1 silently aliases channel 0 (completes normally); I9 decodes to out-of-bounds channel 8 -- a genuine, silent AutoPilot-side dead end. Remote's parsed result (0x200027f0) is never read by anything -- discarded even on success.

Remote FUN_0000e670's 4 call sites (screens 5/9/10) write only the Remote's OWN local per-channel record, never a bulk push or MC4. AutoPilot writes the wire delta into its record but does NOT compute a live target or dirty the persist buffer -- concretely proven (this session's AutoPilot Gap Resolution A) not to arm/commit a move by itself.

TWO distinct Remote triggers: (a) FUN_0000c440's tail -- gated on a clean S|->P... round trip AND a UI-set 'has real programmed data' flag (0x20000fa0, never set by boot alone) -- sends '+' mode=0x62 (crosses AutoPilot's compute+persist threshold, target=start+delta, real move-commit proven end to end) THEN unconditionally MC4; (b) FUN_0000b6f0, a structurally separate periodic pusher (~every 250 ticks via UI pump) that pushes '+' but NEVER sends MC4.

Checked before any ASCII command. 0xE0's field layout is byte-identical to 0xF0 (channel nibble + sign/23-bit magnitude); 0xE0 additionally latches per-channel state to suppress repeat at-limit calls. No dead-man/timeout exists on either side. Remote selects 0xE0 via *0x200018e7==3 (else 0xF0) in FUN_0000be94; sent every UI pump tick including idle heartbeats; stop is implicit (frames simply stop on wheel click).

Remote FUN_00005a8c (sole builder) sends MC<0-3>/MC4 3x with NO ack wait. AutoPilot stores 4 fields per channel; fields 1/3 (CURRENT, MICRO-STEPPING) are display-only (LCD, no driver effect); field 2 (STEPS/S MAX) feeds a real fixed-point step-period computation (24,000,000/value); field 4 (RETURN SPEED) is a table index into a config blob that is blank in this firmware image. MC4 clears 0x20000060, the sole condition unlocking the AutoPilot's main-loop/motor subsystem.

AutoPilot-initiated (not Remote-menu-initiated): sends MT<b0-b3><x>| exactly once per boot from 4 real GPIO connector-presence probes (slot order A->b0,C->b1,B->b2,D->b3). Remote's FUN_00010ce4 reacts, opens Choose-Type screen, assigns 'Not connected' to absent slots. No Remote-side menu entry point exists.

matrix.cross_device_contract: Same mechanism as R7: Remote calls FUN_0000c440 unconditionally once per boot, and again on a debounced reconnect gated by a first-sync latch (0x20000fc9), reset only by a real ~5000-tick radio-silence gap (not a periodic timer).
G/interactive-'+'(C/D): shared 0xb59c-style ack-wait. I9/I1: 6 retries, ~1000-3000 ticks. S/!/bulk-push gate: 'any clean response within ~200 ticks.' MC/MC4/LL1/LL2: sent 3x, NO ack wait at all.

matrix.cross_device_contract: AutoPilot: per-channel-per-mode struct at 0x20001b40 (4 channels x 0x120 bytes), byte-for-byte documented. Remote: mirrored local record at 0x20000b20 (same +0xc/+0x10 delta convention), asserted to load from Remote-local flash at boot but with no specific loader function cited.

matrix.cross_device_contract: AutoPilot-only (3.5mm TRS input, no Remote counterpart in this protocol surface). Digital arm: no debounce/latch, bouncy-insertion risk, fully characterized. Analog arm: exponentially-smoothed PB05/ADC1 filter (0x42a4) with a permanently-zero blend coefficient and a one-shot latch that never clears -- the first boot-time sample is permanently latched for the whole power cycle, explaining the manual's 'connect before power-up = less sensitive' claim exactly.

Covered by R9's AutoPilot-side detail; listed separately here per this task's own explicit reconciliation list. DIR pin identity (PB11/PA09/PB13/PA11, one pin above each channel's STEP pin) and motor enable/disable pin identity (PB16/PB17 enable, PB06/PB07 reset) are resolved; polarity-to-physical-direction and physical Motor1-4 connector mapping are not.
evidence_refs: research/generated/autopilot-replacement-gaps.json (direction control, motor enable/disable GPIO handling, motor configuration)

matrix.cross_device_contract: AutoPilot's D-command/motor-target persistence (flash 0x12000, dirty-flag/save-on-change, NVMCTRL.PARAM-derived page size) is COMPLETE and concretely round-tripped. Remote's MC/MC4 sends expect no ack and no confirmed persistence-mechanism link exists between them and the AutoPilot's own flash-backed config (manual's 'Quick Setup persists' claim not independently confirmed on the wire).
matrix.remaining_unknown: whether MC/MC4 settings have any real AutoPilot-side persistence mechanism at all (pre-existing open item)

matrix.cross_device_contract: AutoPilot: SERCOM2 SPI Master, CS PA15, zero DMA, Stream-derived driver object -- CONFIRMED at MCU-peripheral level; external chip identity confirmed by board inspection (Ai-Thinker Ra-01H/SX1276). Remote: TX wrapper 0x58a8, RX ring buffer 0x20001773 (r/w pointers 0x200017d7/0x200017d8), LoRa/SPI driver chain 0xb440->0x11830->0x11326/0x112e8 -- characterized to the same MCU/radio-chip boundary. Logical packet framing/transport code is identical across variants on BOTH devices; only the AutoPilot's center-frequency constant differs (see RF/build differences, below).
matrix.variant_specific: AutoPilot's own center-frequency .data constant is variant-specific (864MHz/915MHz) -- see dedicated RF/build rows below. Remote's radio driver code is variant-identical; only a display string differs.
matrix.remaining_unknown: exact SX127x register setup (mode/frequency/sync-word/CRC/payload-length) on BOTH devices -- explicitly non-blocking on all four firmware images

matrix.cross_device_contract: '!' response: AutoPilot emits 11 fields; Remote's parser calls its field parser exactly 10 times and marks itself done -- field 11 and its trailing comma are left byte-for-byte unconsumed in the real RX ring buffer, no error on either side. 'I9': decodes to out-of-bounds channel 8 on the AutoPilot side; the Remote's query (6 retries, ~1000-3000 ticks) simply times out. Both are documented, genuine firmware discrepancies -- this project's own standing caution is not to 'fix' either in a harness or replacement.
See variant_specific -- this row exists to record the RF/build facts explicitly, per this task's own instruction, not to imply a behavioral difference.
